brief: Goldman's crypto weekly frames another macro-driven week. Encouraging Fed commentary from Governor Waller took BTC to just below $82.2k on 3 September, retesting the May highs, and was followed by the largest single-day BTC ETF inflow since January at $729m. An upside surprise in the August employment report then reversed the move, taking BTC back to $78k this week and pushing market-implied September rate-hike expectations to about 60%. Flows held up regardless: U.S. spot BTC ETFs took $984m of net inflows last week against $47m of outflows yesterday, leaving year-to-date cumulative flows at -$984m, which the note calls meaningfully narrowing. ETH ETFs took $218m last week and sit at +$840m year-to-date. The rally coincided with stronger demand for gold and CHF against a backdrop of U.S. Treasury intervention in FX and long-dated Treasuries. Since 30 June BTC ranks fourth globally in standard deviation terms and its 50-day average has crossed above its 200-day. Perpetual funding near 1% annualized suggests reduced leveraged long positioning, while 25-delta risk reversals keep a positive skew. Ahead sit treasury buybacks Wednesday, CPI Friday, the CLARITY Act procedural vote on 15 September and the 15-16 September FOMC.
